decks.title: Heart and Circulation — Part 1: The heart and double circulation
goals: Draw and label the internal structure of the heart with its valves and main vessels
Describe the flow of blood through the heart in one cardiac cycle and relate the valves to systole and diastole
Explain double circulation and its advantage in mammals

slides.heading: Circulatory System: Heart, Blood Vessels and Circulation
slides.body_md: Part 1 — the pump at the centre of the circulatory system.

visual.alt: Flow: the heart pumps blood through the blood vessels

slides.narration: Your heart is a muscular pump about the size of your fist. It beats around seventy times a minute, every minute of your life. In this part we open it up, follow the blood through its four chambers, and see why mammals have a double circulation.

slides.heading: Inside the heart
slides.body_md: Four chambers: **right and left auricles** above, **right and left ventricles** below, separated by the **septum**.

slides.narration: In diagrams the right side of the heart is drawn on your left. Blue blood from the body enters the right auricle. Red blood from the lungs enters the left auricle. The left ventricle has the thickest wall because it pumps blood to the whole body.

slides.heading: Chambers and valves

rows: Three flaps; between right auricle and right ventricle
Two flaps; between left auricle and left ventricle
At the bases of the pulmonary artery and aorta
Cords holding the flaps so they do not turn back
Double membrane with fluid; reduces friction

visual.alt: Table of the chambers, valves and coverings of the heart and their features

slides.narration: The valves make the heart a one-way pump. Tricuspid on the right, bicuspid on the left, and semilunar valves where the two great arteries leave. Cords called chordae tendineae stop the flaps being pushed back into the auricles.

slides.narration: Count its flaps.

slides.heading: Main vessels of the heart

visual.alt: Table of the main vessels entering and leaving the heart

slides.narration: Remember the two exceptions. The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood, and the pulmonary veins carry oxygenated blood. An artery is named for carrying blood away from the heart, not for the oxygen it holds.

slides.heading: Worked example 1: following a red blood cell
slides.body_md: Trace one red blood cell from the venae cavae to the aorta.
bullets: Step 1: right side: venae cavae → right auricle → tricuspid → right ventricle → semilunar valve → pulmonary artery.
Step 2: lungs: the cell picks up oxygen and returns in the pulmonary veins.
Step 3: left side: left auricle → bicuspid → left ventricle → semilunar valve → aorta.

visual.alt: Worked flow: venae cavae, right auricle, tricuspid valve, right ventricle, pulmonary artery, lungs, pulmonary veins, left auricle, bicuspid valve, left ventricle, aorta

slides.narration: Follow the blood in order and name each valve as you pass it. A cell entering the right auricle passes four valves before it reaches the aorta: tricuspid, a semilunar valve, bicuspid and another semilunar valve.

slides.heading: The cardiac cycle
slides.body_md: At 75 beats a minute one cycle lasts **0.8 s**: auricles contract, ventricles contract, then the whole heart relaxes.

slides.narration: Contraction is called systole and relaxation diastole. The auricles contract briefly. Then the ventricles contract, closing the tricuspid and bicuspid valves and opening the semilunar valves. Then the whole heart relaxes and fills again.

slides.heading: Valves in systole and diastole

visual.alt: Table of the state of the valves and the movement of blood in each phase of the cardiac cycle

slides.narration: Valves open and close because of pressure. When the ventricles squeeze, the pressure shuts the tricuspid and bicuspid valves, making the lubb sound, and pushes the semilunar valves open. When they relax, the semilunar valves snap shut, making the dub.

slides.heading: Quick check: the second sound
slides.body_md: True or false: the second heart sound, "dub", is made when the semilunar valves close.

slides.heading: Worked example 2: timing and output
slides.body_md: Use the heart rate to find the cycle length and the volume pumped.
bullets: Step 1: cycle length = 60 ÷ 75 = **0.8 s**.
Step 2: at rest, 72 beats × 70 mL per beat = 5040 mL.
Step 3: that is about **5.04 litres** pumped each minute.

visual.alt: Worked table: seventy-five beats a minute gives a cycle of zero point eight seconds; seventy-two beats of seventy millilitres gives about five litres a minute

slides.narration: Divide sixty seconds by the heart rate to get the length of one cycle. Multiply the beats per minute by the amount pumped each beat to get the volume per minute. At rest the heart pumps about five litres a minute, roughly all the blood in the body.

slides.heading: Double circulation
slides.body_md: Blood passes through the heart **twice** in one round: the **pulmonary** circuit and the **systemic** circuit.

slides.heading: Capillaries: where the work is done

nodes.label: Carbon dioxide and wastes diffuse in

visual.alt: Flow: oxygen and food diffuse out of the capillary to the cells, and carbon dioxide and wastes diffuse back in

slides.narration: Capillaries form a fine network in every tissue. Red cells pass through in single file. Oxygen and food diffuse out to the cells, and carbon dioxide and wastes diffuse in. The capillaries then join to form small veins.

slides.heading: The pulse
slides.body_md: The **pulse** is the rhythmic expansion of an artery with each beat of the left ventricle.

rows: An artery lies near the skin over a bone
A large artery lies close to the surface
An artery crosses the bone at the side of the head

visual.alt: Table of three places where the pulse can be felt

slides.narration: Press two fingers lightly on the thumb side of your wrist. Each throb is a surge of blood stretching the artery wall. Pulse rate equals heart rate, about seventy two a minute in a resting adult. Veins have no pulse.

slides.heading: Worked example 1: counting a pulse
slides.body_md: Count for **15 seconds** and multiply by **4**.
bullets: Step 1: at rest, 18 beats × 4 = **72** per minute.
Step 2: after skipping, 31 beats × 4 = **124** per minute.
Step 3: rise = 124 − 72 = **52** beats per minute.

visual.alt: Worked table: eighteen beats in fifteen seconds gives seventy-two a minute; thirty-one beats gives one hundred and twenty-four a minute

slides.narration: Fifteen seconds is a quarter of a minute, so multiply by four. Exercise raises the pulse because the muscles need more oxygen and glucose, and the heart beats faster to deliver them.

slides.heading: The hepatic portal system
slides.body_md: A **portal vein** begins in capillaries of one organ and ends in capillaries of another.

slides.narration: Blood from the intestine goes to the liver before it goes to the heart. The liver stores extra glucose as glycogen, keeps other nutrients, and removes harmful substances. Only then does the blood go on to the rest of the body.

slides.heading: Worked example 2: reading blood samples
slides.body_md: Samples taken an hour after a meal (mg per 100 mL).
bullets: Step 1: glucose falls from 160 to 100: the liver took **60** and stored it as glycogen.
Step 2: urea falls from 30 to 18: the kidney removed **12** into the urine.
Step 3: so the renal vein carries the least urea of any vessel.

slides.narration: Compare the blood going into an organ with the blood coming out. Whatever has changed tells you what the organ did. The liver took up glucose, and the kidney took out urea.

slides.heading: Summary
bullets: Arteries: thick elastic walls, high pressure, away from the heart.
Veins: thin walls, valves, low pressure, towards the heart.
Capillaries: one cell thick; exchange.
Pulse = heart rate; normal blood pressure about 120/80 mm Hg.
Hepatic portal vein takes food-rich blood from the intestine to the liver.

slides.narration: To recap. Each vessel suits its job: arteries for pressure, veins for low pressure return, capillaries for exchange. The pulse and blood pressure are windows into the heart. And blood from the gut always visits the liver first.

bullets: Compare vessels **point against point**: wall, lumen, valves, direction, pressure.
Systolic = ventricles **contract**; diastolic = ventricles **relax**.
Name only the **main vessels** of the heart, liver and kidney.
Hepatic **portal** vein: from the **intestine** to the liver.

notes.title: Circulatory System: Heart, Blood Vessels and Circulation — Notes

sections.heading: 1. Structure of the human heart
sections.body_md:
The heart is a hollow, muscular organ between the lungs, enclosed in a double-layered **pericardium** with **pericardial fluid** (reduces friction, protects).

- **Four chambers:** two thin-walled **auricles (atria)** above, which receive blood; two thick-walled **ventricles** below, which pump it out. The **left ventricle** has the **thickest wall** because it pumps blood to the whole body.
- A muscular **septum** separates the right (deoxygenated) and left (oxygenated) halves.
- **Valves:** **tricuspid** (three flaps) between right auricle and right ventricle; **bicuspid** or mitral (two flaps) between left auricle and left ventricle; **semilunar valves** (three half-moon pockets) at the bases of the pulmonary artery and the aorta. **Chordae tendineae** join the tricuspid and bicuspid flaps to **papillary muscles**, so the flaps cannot turn back into the auricles.

| Main vessel | Joins | Blood |
|---|---|---|
| Superior and inferior **venae cavae** | Body → right auricle | Deoxygenated |
| **Pulmonary artery** | Right ventricle → lungs | Deoxygenated |
| **Pulmonary veins** | Lungs → left auricle | Oxygenated |
| **Aorta** | Left ventricle → body | Oxygenated |

sections.heading: 2. Working of the heart: the cardiac cycle
sections.body_md:
**Systole** = contraction; **diastole** = relaxation. One **cardiac cycle** at 75 beats per minute lasts **0.8 s**:
1. **Auricular systole** (0.1 s): auricles contract and push blood into the ventricles through the open tricuspid and bicuspid valves.
2. **Ventricular systole** (0.3 s): ventricles contract; the **tricuspid and bicuspid close** (first sound, **lubb**); the **semilunar valves open** and blood enters the pulmonary artery and aorta.
3. **Joint diastole** (0.4 s): all chambers relax; the **semilunar valves close** (second sound, **dub**); blood from the veins fills the auricles and flows on into the ventricles.

**Path of blood:** venae cavae → right auricle → tricuspid → right ventricle → semilunar valve → pulmonary artery → lungs → pulmonary veins → left auricle → bicuspid → left ventricle → semilunar valve → aorta → body.

At rest the heart pumps about 70 mL per beat, about 5.04 litres a minute at 72 beats a minute.

sections.heading: 3. Double circulation
sections.body_md:
In mammals blood passes through the heart **twice** in one complete round of the body:
- **Pulmonary circulation:** right ventricle → pulmonary artery → lungs (blood takes up oxygen) → pulmonary veins → left auricle.
- **Systemic circulation:** left ventricle → aorta → all organs → venae cavae → right auricle.

**Advantages:** oxygenated and deoxygenated blood are **kept separate**; the left ventricle sends blood to the body at **high pressure**, while the lungs receive blood at lower pressure. Warm-blooded, active mammals need this rich supply of oxygen.

sections.heading: 4. Arteries, veins and capillaries
sections.body_md:
| Feature | Artery | Vein | Capillary |
|---|---|---|---|
| Carries blood | Away from the heart | Towards the heart | Between arterioles and venules |
| Wall | **Thick**, muscular and elastic | **Thin**, less muscle | **One cell thick** |
| Lumen | Narrow | Wide | Very narrow |
| Valves | Absent (except semilunar at the base) | **Present** | Absent |
| Pressure and flow | High, in jerks (pulse) | Low, smooth | Falling, slow |
| Blood | Oxygenated (except pulmonary artery) | Deoxygenated (except pulmonary veins) | Exchange takes place |
| Position | Mostly deep | Often near the surface | In all tissues |

- **Arteries** withstand high pressure; their elastic walls stretch with each beat.
- **Veins** return blood at low pressure; **valves** prevent backflow, and muscles squeeze the veins. Weak valves in leg veins cause **varicose veins**.
- **Capillaries** are the site of **exchange**: oxygen and food diffuse out, carbon dioxide and wastes diffuse in.

sections.heading: 5. Pulse and blood pressure
sections.body_md:
**Pulse:** the rhythmic expansion of an artery as each surge of blood is pumped by the left ventricle. It is felt where an artery lies near the surface over a bone: the **wrist** (thumb side), the **side of the neck**, the temple. **Pulse rate = heart rate** (about 72 per minute at rest). Veins show no pulse.

**Blood pressure:** the pressure of blood on the walls of the arteries, measured with a **sphygmomanometer** in mm of mercury (mm Hg).
- **120/80 mm Hg** is normal for a young adult.
- **Systolic** (upper figure, 120): highest pressure, while the **ventricles contract**.
- **Diastolic** (lower figure, 80): lowest pressure, while the **ventricles relax**.
- Pressure persistently above about 140/90 mm Hg is **high blood pressure** (hypertension).

key_terms.definition_md: Rhythmic expansion of an artery with each heartbeat.
Arterial pressure during ventricular contraction.
Arterial pressure during ventricular relaxation.
Instrument for measuring blood pressure.

sections.heading: 6. Blood vessels of the liver and kidney
sections.body_md:
| Organ | Vessels bringing blood | Vessel taking blood away |
|---|---|---|
| **Liver** | **Hepatic artery** (oxygenated, from the aorta); **hepatic portal vein** (from the intestine, rich in digested food) | **Hepatic vein** (to the inferior vena cava) |
| **Kidney** | **Renal artery** (from the aorta; contains urea) | **Renal vein** (to the inferior vena cava; least urea) |

**Portal system:** a vein that begins in the capillaries of one organ and ends in the capillaries of another. The **hepatic portal vein** begins in the capillaries of the intestine and ends in the capillaries of the liver.

**Significance of the hepatic portal system:** the liver receives absorbed food **before** the rest of the body, so it can **store excess glucose as glycogen**, store other nutrients, **remove harmful substances** (toxins, drugs) and break down excess amino acids (forming urea), keeping the blood that reaches the heart steady in composition.

key_terms.definition_md: Carries blood from the intestine to the liver.
A vein running from the capillaries of one organ to those of another.
Carries cleaned blood from the kidney.

notes.exam_tips_md:
**Common mistakes**
- Drawing the heart's right side on the right of the page: in a front view it is on **your left**.
- Saying "arteries carry oxygenated blood": arteries carry blood **away from the heart** (the pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood).
- Swapping lubb and dub: **lubb** = tricuspid and bicuspid close; **dub** = semilunar valves close.
- Confusing the **hepatic vein** (leaves the liver) with the **hepatic portal vein** (intestine to liver).
- Naming vessels other than the main ones of the heart, liver and kidney (not required).

**How marks are usually awarded**
- 1 mark: a term (systole, portal system), a valve or vessel, an odd one out **with its category**.
- 2 marks: two differences, a reading explained, a feature with its reason.
- 3 marks: the path of blood with valves, a labelled L.S. of the heart, T.S. of an artery and a vein.

questions.stem_md: The wall of the left ventricle is about three times as thick as the wall of the right ventricle because the left ventricle

options.text_md: receives blood from the whole body
pumps blood to the whole body, which needs a much higher pressure
pumps blood only to the lungs

questions.solution_md: The left ventricle drives blood round the long systemic circuit; the right ventricle pumps only to the nearby lungs — option (b).

options.text_md: They stop the flaps of the tricuspid and bicuspid valves from turning back into the auricles when the ventricles contract
They carry blood to the heart muscle
They divide the heart into right and left halves

questions.solution_md: The cords anchor the valve flaps to papillary muscles, so the flaps cannot be pushed up into the auricles — option (a).

the pleura; the fluid stores glucose

questions.solution_md: Pericardial fluid between the two layers of the pericardium lets the heart beat with little friction and cushions it — option (c).

questions.solution_md: The pulmonary veins return oxygenated blood from the lungs to the left auricle — option (d).

options.text_md: has valves along its whole length
has a wall only one cell thick

questions.solution_md: Like all arteries it carries blood away from the heart, but its blood is deoxygenated, going to the lungs — option (d).

questions.stem_md: A baby is born with a hole in the septum between the two ventricles. The main effect is that

options.text_md: the heart stops pumping blood to the lungs
oxygenated and deoxygenated blood mix, so less oxygen reaches the body
the valves of the heart cannot close

questions.solution_md: The septum keeps the two kinds of blood apart; through a hole they mix and the body receives less oxygen — option (b).

questions.stem_md:
**Assertion (A):** The left ventricle has the thickest wall of all four chambers.

**Reason (R):** It pumps blood into the aorta, which carries blood to all parts of the body.

Choose the correct option.

options.text_md: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution_md: Both are true, and pumping blood round the whole body needs a strong, thick muscular wall — option (c).

questions.stem_md:
**Assertion (A):** The pulmonary artery carries oxygenated blood.

**Reason (R):** Arteries carry blood away from the heart.

Choose the correct option.

options.text_md: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution_md: The assertion is false: the pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood to the lungs. The reason is true — option (b).

questions.stem_md: True or false? The bicuspid valve lies between the right auricle and the right ventricle.
questions.solution_md: False. The bicuspid (mitral) valve is on the left side, between the left auricle and the left ventricle.

questions.stem_md: The valve with two flaps between the left auricle and the left ventricle is the ______ valve.
questions.solution_md: Bicuspid (mitral).

questions.stem_md: Give the biological term: the double-layered membrane that encloses the heart.

answer.model_answer_md: **Pericardium.**

questions.solution_md: Pericardium.

questions.stem_md: Choose the odd one out and name the category to which the other three belong: Tricuspid, Septum, Bicuspid, Semilunar.

answer.model_answer_md: **Septum**; the others are **valves of the heart**.

questions.solution_md: The septum is the wall between the right and left halves.

questions.stem_md: Choose the odd one out and name the category to which the other three belong: Aorta, Pulmonary vein, Pulmonary artery, Left ventricle.

answer.model_answer_md: **Pulmonary artery**; the others **carry or contain oxygenated blood**.

questions.solution_md: The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood.

questions.stem_md: Trace the path of a red blood cell from the venae cavae to the aorta, naming the chambers and valves it passes through.

answer.model_answer_md: Venae cavae → **right auricle** → **tricuspid valve** → **right ventricle** → **semilunar valve** → pulmonary artery → lungs → pulmonary veins → **left auricle** → **bicuspid valve** → **left ventricle** → **semilunar valve** → aorta.

questions.solution_md: Right side, lungs, left side.

marking_scheme.step: Left auricle, bicuspid, left ventricle, aorta with semilunar valves

questions.stem_md: Draw a neat, labelled diagram of the longitudinal section of the human heart. Label the four chambers, the tricuspid and bicuspid valves, the aorta and the pulmonary artery.

answer.model_answer_md: A heart outline with the **right auricle and ventricle** on the viewer's left and the **left auricle and ventricle** on the right; the **left ventricle wall thickest**; the **tricuspid** and **bicuspid** valves with cords between auricles and ventricles; the **pulmonary artery** from the right ventricle and the **aorta** from the left ventricle, each with a semilunar valve; venae cavae and pulmonary veins entering the auricles.

questions.solution_md: Labelled L.S. of the heart.

questions.stem_md: The first heart sound, "lubb", heard through a stethoscope is caused by

options.text_md: the closing of the semilunar valves as the ventricles relax
the closing of the tricuspid and bicuspid valves as the ventricles begin to contract
the opening of the semilunar valves
blood striking the wall of the aorta

questions.solution_md: At the start of ventricular systole the auriculo-ventricular valves snap shut: lubb. Dub is the closing of the semilunar valves — option (b).

questions.stem_md: Which statement describes the valves during ventricular systole?

options.text_md: The tricuspid and bicuspid valves are closed; the semilunar valves are open
The tricuspid and bicuspid valves are open; the semilunar valves are closed
All four valves are closed throughout

questions.solution_md: Contracting ventricles push the auricular valves shut and force the semilunar valves open — option (b).

questions.stem_md: During joint diastole, when all four chambers are relaxed,

options.text_md: blood is pumped into the aorta
the ventricles push blood back into the auricles
blood flows from the veins into the auricles and on into the ventricles

questions.solution_md: With the heart relaxed, the auricular valves are open and the chambers fill from the veins — option (d).

questions.stem_md: A red blood cell enters the right auricle. Counting from there, how many heart valves does it pass through before it reaches the aorta?
questions.solution_md: Tricuspid, semilunar valve of the pulmonary artery, then (after the lungs) bicuspid and semilunar valve of the aorta: four — option (d).

questions.stem_md: True or false? The second heart sound, "dub", is made when the semilunar valves close.
questions.solution_md: True. As the ventricles relax, blood tries to flow back from the arteries and shuts the semilunar valves.

questions.stem_md: A person's heart beats 75 times a minute. How long, in seconds, does one cardiac cycle last?
questions.solution_md: $\dfrac{60}{75} = 0.8$ seconds per cycle.

questions.stem_md: At rest, Rekha's heart beats 72 times a minute and pumps 70 mL of blood at each beat from the left ventricle. How many litres of blood does it pump in one minute?
questions.solution_md: $72 \times 70 = 5040$ mL $= 5.04$ litres per minute.

questions.stem_md: Give the biological term: the phase in which a chamber of the heart contracts.

answer.model_answer_md: **Systole.**

questions.solution_md: Systole.

questions.stem_md: Relate the opening and closing of the heart valves to ventricular systole and diastole.

answer.model_answer_md: In **ventricular systole**, the tricuspid and bicuspid valves **close** and the semilunar valves **open**, so blood enters the arteries. In **diastole**, the semilunar valves **close**, stopping backflow, and the tricuspid and bicuspid **open**, so the ventricles fill.

questions.solution_md: Opposite states in systole and diastole.

questions.stem_md: Double circulation in mammals means that

options.text_md: blood flows in two directions in each vessel
blood passes through the heart twice in one complete round of the body
each organ receives blood from two hearts

questions.solution_md: Blood goes heart → lungs → heart (pulmonary) and heart → body → heart (systemic) — option (c).

questions.stem_md: A harmless dye is injected into the right ventricle of a patient. Which organ will the dye reach first after leaving the heart?
questions.solution_md: The right ventricle pumps blood only into the pulmonary artery, which goes to the lungs (pulmonary circuit) — option (b).

questions.stem_md: Which is an advantage of double circulation?

options.text_md: The heart needs to beat only once a minute
Blood never needs to pass through the lungs
Oxygenated and deoxygenated blood do not mix, and blood is sent to the body at high pressure
Veins can carry blood away from the heart

questions.solution_md: Separate circuits keep the two kinds of blood apart, and the left ventricle can pump at high pressure to the body — option (c).

questions.stem_md: What is double circulation? State one advantage of it to a mammal.

answer.model_answer_md: Blood passes through the heart **twice** in one round: **heart → lungs → heart** (pulmonary) and **heart → body → heart** (systemic). **Advantage:** oxygenated and deoxygenated blood are **kept separate**, so tissues get blood rich in oxygen at high pressure.

questions.solution_md: Two circuits; no mixing.

questions.stem_md: Arteries have thick walls with muscle and elastic fibres because they

options.text_md: carry blood at low pressure back to the heart
carry blood under high pressure in surges from the heart

questions.solution_md: Thick, elastic walls withstand and smooth out the high-pressure surges from the ventricles — option (d).

questions.stem_md: Veins have valves along their length to

options.text_md: let gases pass through the wall
pump blood away from the heart

questions.solution_md: The pocket valves close if blood tries to flow backwards, so it moves only towards the heart — option (c).

questions.stem_md: Food and oxygen pass from blood to the body cells through the capillaries because capillary walls
questions.solution_md: A wall of a single layer of flat cells gives a very short path for diffusion — option (b).

questions.stem_md: After a deep cut on his forearm, bright red blood spurts out of Vikram's wound in jerks, in time with his heartbeat. The vessel cut is most likely
questions.solution_md: Bright red, oxygenated blood under high, pulsing pressure comes from an artery — option (a).

questions.stem_md: A shopkeeper who stands all day develops swollen, twisted veins in his legs. The most likely cause is that

options.text_md: his arteries carry too little blood to the legs
his capillaries have become too thick
the valves in his leg veins have weakened, so blood collects in the veins
his heart pumps blood too fast

questions.solution_md: Leg veins lift blood against gravity; when their valves fail, blood pools and stretches them (varicose veins) — option (c).

questions.stem_md: Under a microscope, a cut blood vessel shows a thin wall with little muscle, a wide, flattened lumen and a pocket-like flap inside. It is most likely
questions.solution_md: A thin wall, a wide lumen and a valve are the marks of a vein — option (d).

questions.stem_md:
**Assertion (A):** Veins have thinner walls than arteries.

**Reason (R):** Veins have valves along their length.

Choose the correct option.

options.text_md: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution_md: Both are true, but the valves do not explain the thin walls; the walls are thin because blood in veins is at low pressure — option (d).

questions.stem_md:
**Assertion (A):** Exchange of materials between blood and tissues takes place across capillaries.

**Reason (R):** Capillary walls are made of thick muscle.

Choose the correct option.

options.text_md: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution_md: The assertion is true. The reason is false: capillary walls are one cell thick, which is what makes exchange possible — option (a).

questions.stem_md: Give reason: oxygen and glucose pass easily from the blood to the cells through capillaries.

answer.model_answer_md: Capillary walls are **only one cell thick**, so substances **diffuse** across them quickly.

questions.solution_md: One cell thick.

questions.stem_md: Give reason: the veins of the legs have many valves.

answer.model_answer_md: Blood in the leg veins must flow **upwards against gravity** at low pressure; the valves **prevent it flowing back** down.

questions.solution_md: Against gravity; no backflow.

questions.stem_md: State two structural differences between an artery and a vein.

answer.model_answer_md:
1. An artery has a **thick, muscular, elastic wall**; a vein has a **thin wall** with little muscle.
2. An artery has a **narrow lumen** and **no valves** along its length; a vein has a **wide lumen** and **valves**.

questions.solution_md: Wall; lumen; valves.

questions.stem_md: Tabulate three differences between an artery and a capillary.

answer.model_answer_md:
| Artery | Capillary |
|---|---|
| **Thick wall** of three layers with muscle | Wall **one cell thick** (endothelium only) |
| Carries blood **away from the heart** to organs | **Connects** small arteries to small veins inside tissues |
| **No exchange** of materials with cells | **Site of exchange** of gases, food and wastes |

questions.solution_md: Wall; position; function.

questions.stem_md: Draw neat, labelled diagrams of the transverse sections of an artery and a vein. Label the lumen and the muscle layer in each.

answer.model_answer_md: An **artery** as a circle with a **thick muscular and elastic wall** around a **small, round lumen**; a **vein** as a flattened, irregular outline with a **thin wall** and a **large lumen**; the **muscle layer** and **lumen** labelled in both.

questions.solution_md: Two T.S. drawn and labelled.

questions.stem_md: The pulse felt at the wrist is

options.text_md: the flow of blood in a vein
the sound of the valves closing
the rhythmic expansion of an artery each time the left ventricle pumps
the contraction of the muscles of the wrist

questions.solution_md: Each beat sends a surge of blood that stretches the elastic artery wall — option (c).

questions.stem_md: In a blood pressure reading of 120/80 mm Hg, the figure 80 is the

options.text_md: diastolic pressure, when the ventricles relax
systolic pressure, when the ventricles contract

questions.solution_md: The lower figure is the diastolic pressure in the arteries while the ventricles are relaxed — option (a).

questions.stem_md: A pulse cannot be felt in a vein because

options.text_md: blood in veins flows smoothly at low pressure, without surges
veins carry no blood between beats

questions.solution_md: By the time blood reaches the veins, the surges of each heartbeat have died away — option (a).

questions.stem_md: Nikhil counts 18 beats of his pulse in 15 seconds. What is his pulse rate per minute?
questions.solution_md: $18 \times \dfrac{60}{15} = 72$ beats per minute.

questions.stem_md:
**Assertion (A):** Systolic pressure is higher than diastolic pressure.

**Reason (R):** Systolic pressure is recorded while the ventricles are relaxed.

Choose the correct option.

options.text_md: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution_md: The assertion is true. The reason is false: systolic pressure is recorded while the ventricles contract; diastolic pressure while they relax — option (a).

questions.stem_md: True or false? A person's pulse rate is normally the same as the heart rate.
questions.solution_md: True. Each contraction of the left ventricle produces one pulse wave.

questions.stem_md: Blood pressure is measured with an instrument called a ______.
questions.solution_md: Sphygmomanometer.

questions.stem_md: Give the biological term: the pressure of blood in the arteries while the ventricles are relaxing.

answer.model_answer_md: **Diastolic pressure.**

questions.solution_md: Diastolic pressure.

questions.stem_md: Give reason: counting the pulse at the wrist tells a doctor the heart rate.

answer.model_answer_md: Each **contraction of the left ventricle** sends **one pulse wave** along the arteries, so pulse rate **equals** heart rate.

questions.solution_md: One wave per beat.

questions.stem_md: Nurse Joseph records a blood pressure of 120/80 mm Hg. What does each number mean?

answer.model_answer_md: **120** is the **systolic pressure**: the highest pressure in the arteries, when the **ventricles contract**. **80** is the **diastolic pressure**: the lowest pressure, when the **ventricles relax**. Both are in millimetres of mercury.

questions.solution_md: Systolic; diastolic.

questions.stem_md: Rekha's heart pumps 5.04 litres of blood a minute at 72 beats a minute. A trained athlete's heart pumps the same volume at rest with only 56 beats a minute. How many millilitres does the athlete's heart pump at each beat?
questions.solution_md: $5.04$ litres $= 5040$ mL; $\dfrac{5040}{56} = 90$ mL per beat: a stronger heart pumps more at each beat.

questions.stem_md: The hepatic portal vein carries blood

options.text_md: from the liver to the heart
from the heart to the liver
from the intestine to the liver
from the kidney to the liver

questions.solution_md: It collects blood rich in absorbed food from the intestine and takes it to the liver — option (c).

questions.stem_md: A portal vein is one that

options.text_md: carries blood straight from the heart to an organ
has no valves and no wall
begins in the capillaries of one organ and ends in the capillaries of another

questions.solution_md: The hepatic portal vein starts in capillaries of the intestine and breaks up into capillaries in the liver — option (d).

questions.stem_md: An hour after a sweet, starchy meal, which blood vessel will carry blood with the most glucose?
questions.solution_md: Glucose absorbed from the intestine travels in the hepatic portal vein; the liver stores the excess before blood leaves in the hepatic vein — option (a).

questions.stem_md: Blood samples are taken from four vessels of a healthy person. Which sample will contain the least urea?
questions.solution_md: The kidney removes urea, so blood leaving it in the renal vein has the least; the hepatic vein carries urea newly made by the liver — option (a).

questions.stem_md:
**Assertion (A):** Blood from the intestine passes through the liver before it reaches the heart.

**Reason (R):** The liver stores excess glucose as glycogen and removes harmful substances from the absorbed food.

Choose the correct option.

options.text_md: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution_md: Both are true, and the liver's work on absorbed food explains why the hepatic portal vein delivers blood there first — option (c).

questions.stem_md: Give the biological term: an arrangement in which a vein carries blood from the capillaries of one organ to the capillaries of another organ.

answer.model_answer_md: **Portal system** (for example, the hepatic portal system).

questions.solution_md: Portal system.

questions.stem_md: Choose the odd one out and name the category to which the other three belong: Hepatic artery, Renal artery, Hepatic vein, Hepatic portal vein.

answer.model_answer_md: **Renal artery**; the others are **blood vessels of the liver**.

questions.solution_md: The renal artery supplies the kidney.

questions.stem_md: Give reason: digested food from the intestine is first taken to the liver and not straight to the heart.

answer.model_answer_md: The liver **stores excess glucose as glycogen** and **removes toxins** from the absorbed food before the blood reaches the rest of the body.

questions.solution_md: Liver processes absorbed food.

marking_scheme.step: Liver stores excess and removes toxins

questions.stem_md: Name the two blood vessels that bring blood to the liver and the one that takes blood away from it.

answer.model_answer_md: Blood is brought by the **hepatic artery** (oxygenated, from the aorta) and the **hepatic portal vein** (rich in digested food, from the intestine). It is taken away by the **hepatic vein** to the inferior vena cava.

questions.solution_md: Hepatic artery, hepatic portal vein; hepatic vein.

marking_scheme.step: Hepatic artery and hepatic portal vein

questions.stem_md:
Select the correct terms to fill in the blanks: [pericardium, auricles, ventricles, bicuspid, tricuspid, chordae tendineae, left ventricle, right ventricle]

The heart lies inside a double-layered membrane, the (a) ______. Its two thin-walled upper chambers, the (b) ______, receive blood from the veins. The valve between the left upper and left lower chambers is the (c) ______ valve, and its flaps are held in place by cords called (d) ______. The chamber with the thickest wall is the (e) ______.
questions.solution_md: (a) pericardium; (b) auricles; (c) bicuspid; (d) chordae tendineae; (e) left ventricle.

questions.stem_md:
Select the correct terms to fill in the blanks: [capillaries, valves, pulse, sphygmomanometer, stethoscope, hepatic portal vein, hepatic vein, arteries]

Veins contain (a) ______ that prevent the backflow of blood. Food and oxygen leave the blood across the walls of the (b) ______. The throb felt at the wrist with each heartbeat is the (c) ______. Blood pressure is measured with a (d) ______. Blood rich in digested food reaches the liver in the (e) ______.
questions.solution_md: (a) valves; (b) capillaries; (c) pulse; (d) sphygmomanometer; (e) hepatic portal vein.

questions.stem_md: Study the diagram of the heart and match each lettered part with its function.

match_right.text_md: Carries deoxygenated blood to the lungs
Stops blood flowing back from the pulmonary artery into the right ventricle
Stops blood flowing back from the right ventricle into the right auricle
Hold the valve flaps so that they cannot turn back into the auricle
Pumps oxygenated blood into the aorta at high pressure

questions.solution_md: A left ventricle; B tricuspid valve; C pulmonary artery; D chordae tendineae; E semilunar valve of the pulmonary artery.

children.stem_md: How long does one cardiac cycle of Mira's heart last, in seconds?
Which valves close to make the "lubb" and which to make the "dub"?

answer.model_answer_md: **Lubb:** the **tricuspid and bicuspid** valves close as the ventricles begin to contract. **Dub:** the **semilunar valves** close as the ventricles relax and blood presses back from the arteries.

children.stem_md: According to the diagram, for how long are the semilunar valves open in each cycle, and where does blood go during this time?

answer.model_answer_md: For **0.3 s**, while the **ventricles contract**. Blood is pumped from the right ventricle into the **pulmonary artery** and from the left ventricle into the **aorta**.

marking_scheme.step: Into the pulmonary artery and aorta

children.stem_md: Why are the chordae tendineae especially important during ventricular systole?

answer.model_answer_md: During ventricular systole the pressure in the ventricles is high. The chordae tendineae **hold the tricuspid and bicuspid flaps** so they are **not pushed back into the auricles**, preventing backflow.

children.stem_md: Some weeks later the doctor hears a soft swishing sound after each "lubb" and suspects that the bicuspid valve is not closing properly. Explain what happens to the blood and how the body is affected.

answer.model_answer_md: When the left ventricle contracts, some blood **leaks back** through the faulty **bicuspid valve** into the **left auricle**; the swishing sound is this backflow. **Less blood** goes into the aorta at each beat, so the heart must **beat faster or harder** to supply the body, and Mira may feel **tired and breathless**.

children.solution_md: Backflow into the left auricle; less output.

answer.model_answer_md:
**(a)** 72

questions.passage_md: A few hours after birth, baby Aarav's lips and fingertips looked bluish. Tests showed a hole in the septum between his two ventricles. His doctor said the hole could be closed by surgery.

answer.model_answer_md:
**(a)** The **muscular wall** that separates the **right and left** halves of the heart.

**(b)** **Oxygenated** blood from the left ventricle and **deoxygenated** blood from the right ventricle **mix** through the hole, so the blood sent to the body carries **less oxygen**, giving a bluish tinge.

**(c)** **Pulmonary circuit:** the right ventricle pumps deoxygenated blood through the **pulmonary artery** to the lungs; oxygenated blood returns through the **pulmonary veins** to the left auricle. **Systemic circuit:** the left ventricle pumps oxygenated blood through the **aorta** to the body; deoxygenated blood returns through the **venae cavae** to the right auricle.

**(d)** The **right side** (right auricle and ventricle). Deoxygenated blood is brought from the body by the **superior and inferior venae cavae**.

**(e)** Mammals are **warm-blooded** and very active, so their cells need a **large, steady supply of oxygen** to release energy. Keeping the two kinds of blood apart sends **fully oxygenated blood** to the tissues.

questions.solution_md:
**(a)** Wall between the two halves.

**(b)** Mixing of blood.

**(c)** Two circuits with vessels.

**(d)** Right side; venae cavae.

**(e)** High oxygen need.
